articles.title: Why AI Could Create More Places Like Youngstown, Ohio
articles.summary: The story of Youngstown, Ohio, is often seen as a story about the past. But it’s time to start looking at the Rust Belt city as a warning about the future. As the artificial intelligence revolution unfolds, debates about its impact on the American economy often hinge on the belief that if the technology creates more jobs than it destroys, it will be a success. articles.summary: The 2026 midterm election results rebuked President Donald Trump’s failures on the economy and, in several competitive races, his immigration agenda. Latino voters who backed him in 2024 swung back to Democrats, helping deliver the politically unthinkable. Texas elected its first Democratic senator since 1988 and its first Latina governor , while Democrats won governorships in all four southern border states and every southern border congressional district. articles.title: Trump Gutted USAID. Congo Pays the Price in an Ebola Epidemic
articles.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is reeling from an outbreak of Ebola that is estimated to have killed nearly 5,400 people. The World Health Organization (WHO) has described it as “the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported” in the country. The outbreak was first detected in Mongbwalu , a gold-mining town of around 130,000 people in Ituri province in northeastern Congo, after the WHO was alerted on May 5 about an unusual cluster of illness and deaths. articles.title: Van Hollen Challenges Schumer for Senate Majority Leader
articles.summary: Chris Van Hollen will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate Majority Leader in the new Congress, marking the first time in decades that the race will be contested. articles.title: How Movies About Tech Turned Dystopian
articles.summary: In 2014, a film about a prickly, arrogant inventor trying to build a “machine that can solve any problem” arrived in theaters. From the vantage point of 2026, the story sounds unsettling, even dystopian.
